title: OpenCode HTTP API Discovery
summary: Authenticated Basic HTTP access to the already-running local OpenCode server was verified by the operator. The OpenAPI document at /doc returned HTTP 200, content-type application/json, and exposed 113 paths, including /session, /session/status, /session/{sessionID}/message, /session/{sessionID}/abort, /event, /api/session/{sessionID}/prompt, and /api/session/{sessionID}/wait. This confirms that ForgePilot MCP can move from terminal-output inference toward explicit OpenCode HTTP session lifecycle observation.
caveats: The successful authenticated /doc probe was executed by the operator locally because the MCP terminal wrapper blocked commands that handled OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD, even when values were not printed.
The discovery did not create sessions, send prompts, abort sessions, mutate files, or start OpenCode.
Endpoint semantics such as /api/session/{sessionID}/wait and /event still require packeted read-only implementation and verification before use as evidence.
Credentials are available to the MCP service environment through OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME and OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD, but secret values were not printed or committed.
boundaries: This checkpoint records discovery only and does not authorize execution.
No runner start endpoint was contacted by this checkpoint.
No OpenCode HTTP prompt was submitted by this checkpoint.
No approval was consumed and no local execution clearance was created.
Future HTTP MCP tools must treat start acceptance and completion as separate observations.
